chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad and Muhammad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Maysarah, from Abd al-Aziz, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to him; does he pay zakat on it? He said: 'For every debt that he leaves behind, when he intends to collect it, zakat is obligatory upon him. And whatever he is unable to collect, there is no zakat upon him.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And there is no zakat on the lender, and on the borrower, his zakat is obligatory as long as it is in his hand. When it returns to its owner and the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory upon him. What indicates this is what he narrated:'

key_terms.حَالَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: The lunar year passed over it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat for money owed to you as a debt?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the practical jurisprudence of zakat on debts, distinguishing between collectible and uncollectible amounts, a ruling foundational to Shia fiqh. Al-Tusi’s commentary further clarifies the dual obligation: the borrower pays on the principal while in possession, while the lender’s liability commences only upon repayment and the completion of the lunar year (hawl). This ensures that zakat is not levied on wealth that remains out of the creditor's effective control.
